text.p: Norwegian offshore and construction group Aker ASA is expected to post an eight-month profit before tax of 309 million crowns, according to seven analysts polled by Reuters.
The comparative 1995 figure was 451 million crowns.

Only one analyst recommended to buy Aker shares while two said sell. The remaining four said hold, but some said they may downgrade the recommendation to sell. Most brokerhouses were cautious ahead of the proposed merger with investment group Research Group International ASA.

Last month's Sleipner settlement will be reflected in the eight-month result. Aker had previously set aside 300 million crowns and another nearly 100 million crowns are expected to be booked under operational costs in the result.
Aker subsidiary Norwegian Contractors (NC) was building Sleipner's concrete gravity base when it sank in a fjord near Stavanger in August 1991.
Aker will present the result on Thursday at 9 a.m. (0700gmt)
